sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: create_specifier_set
tools.description: Create a SpecifierSet object from a string or iterable of specifiers. specifiers: A string representation of a specifier or a comma-separated list of specifiers, e.g. '>=3.0,!=3.1' -> SpecifierSet object serialized as string. prereleases: Whether to accept prerelease versions if applicable.

tools.name: create_version
tools.description: Create a Version object from a version string. version_string: A string representation of a version conforming to PEP 440, e.g. '1.0a5' -> "<Version('1.0a5')>".

tools.name: create_specifier
tools.description: Create a Specifier object from a specifier string. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g. '>=1.0.0' -> Specifier object. prereleases: Whether to allow pre-release versions.

tools.name: create_marker
tools.description: Parse and create a Marker object from a marker string. marker_string: The string representation of a marker expression, e.g. 'python_version > "3.6"' -> "<Marker('python_version > "3.6"')>".

tools.name: specifier_set_to_range
tools.description: Convert a SpecifierSet to its equivalent VersionRange. specifiers: A string representation of version specifiers, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0' -> '[1.0, 2.0.dev0)'.

tools.name: filter_with_version_range
tools.description:
Yield items from iterable whose version falls inside the range.
    
    Args:
        version_range_spec (str): A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet
        iterable (list[str]): An iterable of version strings
        prereleases (bool | None, optional): Whether to include pre-release versions; None uses PEP 440 default behavior
    
    Returns:
        list[str]: Items from iterable whose version falls inside the range
        
    Example:
        >>> filter_with_version_range(">=1.0,<2.0", ["0.9", "1.5", "2.0"])
        ['1.5']

tools.name: is_specifier_set_unsatisfiable
tools.description:
Check whether this specifier set can never be satisfied.
    
    Returns True if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously.
    
    Args:
        specifiers (str): A string representation of version specifiers
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if the specifier set is unsatisfiable, False otherwise
        
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_unsatisfiable(">=2.0,<1.0")
        True

tools.name: is_version_range_empty
tools.description: Check if a VersionRange contains no versions. range_string: A string representation of a version range, e.g., '>=1.0,<2.0' -> True. prereleases: Whether pre-releases are allowed. If False, ranges containing only pre-releases are considered empty.

tools.name: is_version_prerelease
tools.description: Determine if a Version is a pre-release version. version: A version string to check if it is a pre-release version -> true if pre-release, false otherwise.

tools.name: specifier_contains_version
tools.description:
Check if a Specifier contains a specific version.
    
    Args:
        specifier: A version specifier string, e.g., '>=1.2.3'
        version: The version string to check against the specifier
        prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this Specifier. 
                     If None, follows PEP 440 defaults.
    
    Returns:
        True if the version is contained in the specifier, False otherwise.
        
    Example:
        >>> specifier_contains_version('>=1.2.3', '1.2.3')
        True

tools.name: filter_with_specifier
tools.description:
Filter items in the given iterable, that match the specifier.
    
    :param specifier: A version specifier string
    :param iterable: An iterable of version strings or Version instances
    :param prereleases: Whether to include prereleases in the result
    
    >>> list(Specifier(">=1.2.3").filter(["1.2", "1.3", "1.5a1"]))
    ['1.3']

tools.name: specifier_set_contains_version
tools.description:
Check if a SpecifierSet contains a specific version.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set (str): A string representation of the SpecifierSet (e.g., '>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1')
        version (str): The version string to check against the SpecifierSet
        prereleases (bool | None, optional): Whether or not to match prereleases with this SpecifierSet. 
                                             If None, follows PEP 440 recommendations.
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if the version is contained in the SpecifierSet, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> specifier_set_contains_version('>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1', '1.2.3')
        True

tools.name: create_full_version_range
tools.description: Create a VersionRange that accepts all PEP 440 versions. admit_arbitrary: whether to admit arbitrary strings as versions; prereleases: whether to include pre-release versions.

tools.name: create_empty_version_range
tools.description: Create a VersionRange that accepts no versions. prereleases: Whether pre-release versions should be considered. -> A dictionary representing the empty VersionRange.

tools.name: create_singleton_version_range
tools.description: Create a VersionRange that only accepts a single specific version. version: A PEP 440 compliant version string, e.g. '1.0' -> VersionRange singleton for 1.0. prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions; if None, uses the default behavior. Example: create_singleton_version_range('1.0') -> '1.0'.

tools.name: canonicalize_version_string
tools.description: Return a canonical form of a version string. version: A version string to canonicalize, e.g. '1.0.0' -> '1'. strip_trailing_zero: Whether to strip trailing zeros from the release segment, e.g. '1.0.0' with strip_trailing_zero=False -> '1.0.0'.

tools.name: get_version_pre_release
tools.description:
Get the pre-release segment of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the pre-release segment from
    
    >>> print(get_version_pre_release("1.2.3"))
    None
    >>> get_version_pre_release("1.2.3a1")
    ('a', 1)
    >>> get_version_pre_release("1.2.3b1")
    ('b', 1)
    >>> get_version_pre_release("1.2.3rc1")
    ('rc', 1)

tools.name: get_version_release
tools.description:
Get the release components of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the release components from
    
    >>> get_version_release("1.2.3")
    (1, 2, 3)

tools.name: get_version_post_release
tools.description:
Get the post-release number of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the post-release number from
    
    >>> print(get_version_post_release("1.2.3"))
    None
    >>> get_version_post_release("1.2.3.post1")
    1

tools.name: is_version_postrelease
tools.description: Check if a Version is a post-release version. version: A version string to check if it is a post-release version -> true if post-release, false otherwise.

tools.name: get_version_epoch
tools.description:
Get the epoch of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the epoch from -> The epoch of the version.
    
    >>> get_version_epoch("2.0.0")
    0
    >>> get_version_epoch("1!2.0.0")
    1

tools.name: get_version_public
tools.description: Get the public portion of a version. version: A version string to extract the public portion from -> The public portion without local version identifiers.

tools.name: get_version_base
tools.description: Get the base version of a version. version: A version string to extract the base version from -> '1.2.3'.

tools.name: get_version_dev
tools.description: Get the development number of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the development number from -> The development number, or None if not a development version.

tools.name: get_version_local
tools.description: Get the local version segment of a version. version: A version string to parse, e.g. '1.2.3+abc' -> 'abc'.

tools.name: is_version_devrelease
tools.description: Check if a Version is a development release. version: A version string to check if it's a development release -> true if development release, false otherwise.

tools.name: get_version_minor
tools.description:
Get the minor version component. version: A version string to parse and extract the minor version from
    
    >>> get_version_minor("1.2.3")
    2
    >>> get_version_minor("1")
    0

tools.name: get_version_micro
tools.description:
Get the micro version component. version: A version string to parse and extract the micro version from
    
    >>> get_version_micro("1.2.3")
    3
    >>> get_version_micro("1")
    0

tools.name: get_version_major
tools.description: Get the major version component. version: A version string to parse and extract the major version from, e.g. '1.2.3' -> 1.

tools.name: parse_version_string
tools.description:
Parse the given version string.
    
    This is identical to the Version constructor.
    
    >>> parse_version_string('1.0.dev1')
    '1.0.dev1'
    
    :param version: The version string to parse.
    :raises ValueError: When the version string is not a valid version.

tools.name: normalize_pre_release
tools.description: Normalize the pre-release segment of a version string. letter: The pre-release identifier to normalize, e.g. 'alpha' -> 'a'.

tools.name: check_specifier_set_subset
tools.description:
Check if all versions matching this set also match another set.
    
    Args:
        specifiers: A string representation of the specifier set to check
        other_specifiers: A string representation of the other specifier set to compare against
    
    Returns:
        True if every version matching the first set also matches the second set, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> check_specifier_set_subset(">=3.12,<3.13", ">=3.12")
        True

tools.name: check_specifier_set_disjoint
tools.description:
Check if two SpecifierSets share no matching versions.
    
    Args:
        specifier1: First specifier string to form a SpecifierSet
        specifier2: Second specifier string to form a SpecifierSet
    
    Returns:
        True if the sets share no matching versions, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> check_specifier_set_disjoint("<3.12", ">=3.12")
        True

tools.name: check_specifier_set_superset
tools.description:
Return whether every version matching other also matches this set.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set (str): The specifier set to check against
        other_set (str): The other specifier set to compare with
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if specifier_set is a superset of other_set, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> check_specifier_set_superset(">=3.12", ">=3.12,<3.13")
        True

tools.name: check_version_range_subset
tools.description: Check if all versions in range1 are also in range2. range1: first version range specifier string, range2: second version range specifier string to check if range1 is a subset of this. >>> check_version_range_subset('>=1.5,<1.8', '>=1.0,<2.0') -> True

tools.name: check_version_range_superset
tools.description: Check if all versions in range2 are also in range1. range1: a version range specifier string, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0'. range2: another version range specifier string to check if it's a subset of range1.

tools.name: check_version_range_disjoint
tools.description:
Check if two version ranges share no common versions.
    
    Args:
        version_range1 (str): A version range specifier string (e.g., '>=1.0,<2.0')
        version_range2 (str): Another version range specifier string (e.g., '>=2.0,<3.0')
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if the ranges are disjoint (share no common versions), False otherwise
        
    Example:
        >>> check_version_range_disjoint('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=2.0,<3.0')
        True

tools.name: intersect_version_ranges
tools.description:
Return a VersionRange containing versions present in both ranges.
    
    Args:
        range1 (str): First version range specifier string
        range2 (str): Second version range specifier string
    
    Returns:
        str: A string representation of the intersected version range
    
    Example:
        >>> intersect_version_ranges(">=1.0", "<2.0")
        '>=1.0,<2.0'

tools.name: union_version_ranges
tools.description:
Return a VersionRange containing versions in either range.
    
    Both operands must share the same configured pre-release policy.
    
    Args:
        range1 (str): First version range specification
        range2 (str): Second version range specification
    
    Returns:
        str: String representation of the unioned version range
        
    Example:
        >>> union_version_ranges(">=1.0,<2.0", ">=3.0,<4.0")
        '>=1.0,<2.0 | >=3.0,<4.0'

tools.name: difference_version_ranges
tools.description:
Return a VersionRange containing versions in the first range but not the second.
    
    Args:
        first_range (str): A version specifier string representing the first version range
        second_range (str): A version specifier string representing the second version range to exclude from the first
    
    Returns:
        str: A string representation of the resulting VersionRange
    
    Example:
        >>> difference_version_ranges(">=1.0", ">=2.0")
        '>=1.0,<2.0'

tools.name: get_specifier_operator
tools.description: Get the operator part of a Specifier. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g. '==1.2.3' -> '=='

tools.name: get_specifier_version
tools.description: Get the version part of a Specifier. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g. '==1.2.3' -> '1.2.3'.

tools.name: canonicalize_package_name
tools.description: Canonicalize a package name according to PEP 503. name: The name to normalize. validate: Check whether the name is a valid distribution name. >>> canonicalize_package_name('Django') 'django'

tools.name: is_package_name_normalized
tools.description: Check if a package name is normalized. name: The package name to check for normalization, e.g. 'requests' -> true.

tools.name: evaluate_marker
tools.description: Evaluate a marker expression against an environment. marker: A marker expression to evaluate, e.g. 'python_version >= "3.6"' -> True. environment: Mapping containing keys and values to override the detected environment. context: The context in which the marker is evaluated, which influences what marker names are considered valid. Accepted values are "metadata" (default), "lock_file", and "requirement".

tools.name: get_default_marker_environment
tools.description:
Get the default marker environment for the current Python process.
    
    Returns a dictionary containing environment markers like python_version, platform_system, etc.
    These markers are used by packaging tools to evaluate environment markers in requirements.
    
    Example:
        >>> env = get_default_marker_environment()
        >>> env['python_version']
        '3.9'

tools.name: resolve_dependency_group
tools.description:
Resolve a dependency group to a list of requirements.
    
    :param dependency_groups: A mapping of dependency group names to their requirements
    :param group: The name of the group to resolve
    :example: resolve_dependency_group({"backend": ["flask", "sqlalchemy"]}, "backend") -> ["flask", "sqlalchemy"]

tools.name: lookup_dependency_group
tools.description:
Lookup a group name, returning the parsed dependency data for that group.
    This will not resolve includes.
    
    :param dependency_groups: Mapping of dependency group names to their definitions
    :param group: the name of the group to lookup
    :example: lookup_dependency_group({"dev": ["pytest", "black"]}, "dev") -> ["pytest", "black"]
